claims.claim_text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a cost-effective approach to improving large language model output so it remains relevant, accurate, and useful in various contexts.

claims.claim_text: The difference between RAG and fine-tuning is that RAG lets an LLM query an external data source while fine-tuning trains an LLM on domain-specific data.

claims.evidence_span: Fine-tuning increases a model’s familiarity with the intended domain and output requirements, while RAG assists the model in generating relevant, high-quality outputs.

claims.evidence_span: A blog by Lewis and three of the paper’s coauthors said developers can implement the process with as few as five lines of code.

claims.claim_text: Patrick Lewis led the author team of the 2020 paper that coined the term retrieval-augmented generation.
